Match the ABCD assessment component in List I with its clinical parameter in List II:

List I:
(A) Anthropometric
(B) Biochemical
(C) Clinical
(D) Dietary

List II:
(I) Height, weight, Body Mass Index (BMI), and Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC)
(II) Serum hemoglobin, serum albumin, blood glucose, and lipid profiles
(III) Inspection of eyes for Bitot spots, tongue for glossitis, and skin for pallor
(IV) 24-hour dietary recall, food frequency questionnaires, and diet history

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

Anthropometry measures body dimensions, Biochemical measures laboratory blood markers, Clinical inspects physical signs, and Dietary analyzes food intake.

topic: Preservative Mechanism of High Salt in Pickling
questionText: What dual preservative effect does 15-20% salt concentration provide in traditional Indian pickles?

options.text: Turns vegetables into toxic chemicals
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Dissolves all food nutrients permanently
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Neutralizes all natural fruit flavors
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Draws water out of food tissues via osmosis, lowers water activity, and induces plasmolysis in spoilage bacteria
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Preservative Mechanism of High Salt in Pickling.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Nutrition, Food Science and Technology (Preservative Mechanism of High Salt in Pickling):
Draws water out of food tissues via osmosis, lowers water activity, and induces plasmolysis in spoilage bacteria

Detailed Context:
High salt concentration reduces water activity and causes osmotic plasmolysis, suppressing bacterial decomposition.
Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Match the micronutrient deficiency in List I with its clinical manifestation in List II:

List I:
(A) Iron Deficiency
(B) Vitamin A Deficiency
(C) Iodine Deficiency
(D) Vitamin D Deficiency

List II:
(I) Microcytic hypochromic anemia, cognitive blunting, fatigue, and koilonychia
(II) Night blindness (Nyctalopia), conjunctival xerosis, Bitot spots, and keratomalacia
(III) Endemic goitre, mental subnormality, and congenital cretinism in neonates
(IV) Rickets in growing children (craniotabes, rachitic rosary, bow legs) and osteomalacia in adults

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Micronutrient Deficiencies and Clinical Manifestations.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Micronutrient Deficiencies and Clinical Manifestations (Nutrition, Food Science and Technology):
Iron causes microcytic anemia; Vitamin A causes night blindness and keratomalacia; Iodine causes goitre and cretinism; Vitamin D causes rickets.
Hence Option C is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Read the following case study on managing Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in an inpatient facility and answer the questions that follow:

Two-year-old Meena is brought to a district hospital Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre (NRC) in a state of severe emaciation. Clinical assessment reveals severe wasting (Weight-for-Height Z-score < -3 SD), Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) of 10.8 cm, hypoglycemia, and hypothermia (body temperature 35.2°C). The medical officer and clinical nutritionist implement the 10-step WHO protocol for the management of Severe Acute Malnutrition:
1. Phase 1 (Stabilization, Days 1-2): Rewarming the child, administering 10% glucose to correct hypoglycemia, providing ReSoMal for dehydration, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and cautious 2-hourly feeding with F-75 starter formula (75 kcal and 0.9 g protein/100 mL).
2. Phase 2 (Transition & Rehabilitation, Days 3-14): As appetite returns and infections subside, Meena transitions to F-100 catch-up formula (100 kcal and 2.9 g protein/100 mL) and Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF), achieving rapid catch-up growth (> 10 g/kg/day weight gain).
3. Maternal Counseling: Educating the mother on energy-dense complementary feeding using locally available sprouted lentils and groundnuts before discharge.

Question: Why is specialized ReSoMal (Rehydration Solution for Malnutrition) utilized instead of standard adult ORS for children with SAM?

options.text: Standard ORS contains antibiotics that interfere with renal function in severely malnourished children
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: ReSoMal contains lower sodium with higher potassium and magnesium to prevent fatal fluid overload and heart failure
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for ReSoMal Composition Distinction.

options.text: ReSoMal is completely sugar-free to prevent severe osmotic diarrhea and rapid fluid shifts
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: ReSoMal is designed exclusively for rapid intravenous rehydration to bypass gastrointestinal malabsorption
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Nutrition, Food Science and Technology (ReSoMal Composition Distinction):
ReSoMal contains lower sodium with higher potassium and magnesium to prevent fatal fluid overload and heart failure

Detailed Context:
Children with SAM have altered cellular sodium-potassium pumps and excess body sodium; standard ORS high-sodium content can cause fluid retention and heart failure. ReSoMal addresses this with lower sodium and increased potassium and magnesium concentrations.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
